surface: Workspace agent reading uploaded PDF documents
impact: Exfiltration of workspace data via web-search tool
summary: Hidden instructions in an uploaded PDF directed the Notion agent to collect workspace content and send it to an attacker URL through its web-search tool.

surface: CRM agent processing attacker-submitted lead form fields
impact: Exfiltration of CRM lead data to an attacker-controlled domain
summary: Instructions placed in a Web-to-Lead description field were executed when an employee asked Agentforce about the lead, leaking CRM records to an expired domain still on the CSP allowlist.

surface: Browser agent summarizing web page content
impact: Account takeover actions and data exfiltration on behalf of the user
summary: Text embedded in a web page (for example a Reddit comment) was treated as user instructions by the Comet agent, which then browsed to the user's accounts and leaked credentials and one-time codes.

surface: Assistant reading calendar invitations and email
impact: Control of smart-home devices, geolocation leak and spam on victim's behalf
summary: Instructions hidden in calendar invitation titles were executed when the victim asked Gemini about their schedule, triggering agent actions across Workspace and Google Home.
sourceName: SafeBreach (Ben Nassi, Stav Cohen, Or Yair)

surface: Assistant reading documents from a connected cloud drive
impact: Zero-click exfiltration of API keys and documents via rendered image URL
summary: A shared document containing hidden instructions caused ChatGPT to search the victim's Drive for secrets and leak them through a rendered image request to an attacker server.

surface: IDE agent consuming content fetched through MCP tools
impact: Arbitrary code execution on the developer machine
summary: Prompt injection delivered through an MCP tool (for example a Slack message) made the Cursor agent write a malicious .cursor/mcp.json, which ran attacker commands without approval (CVE-2025-54135).

surface: Project-scoped MCP configuration in a shared repository
impact: Persistent remote code execution on collaborators' machines
summary: Once a benign MCP server entry was approved, its command could be silently swapped in the repository for a malicious one and executed on every open without re-prompting (CVE-2025-54136).

surface: MCP client proxy connecting to remote MCP servers
impact: Arbitrary OS command execution on the MCP client host
summary: A malicious remote MCP server could return a crafted OAuth authorization endpoint that mcp-remote passed to a shell, executing attacker commands on the client machine (CVE-2025-6514).

surface: Coding agent querying a production database via MCP
impact: Exfiltration of private database tables through agent-issued SQL
summary: A support ticket containing instructions was read by a Cursor agent connected to the Supabase MCP server with service-role privileges, which then dumped a secrets table into a public ticket field.

surface: MCP server exposing filesystem access to an agent
impact: Sandbox escape and file access outside allowed directories
summary: Path validation flaws in the reference Filesystem MCP server allowed reads and writes outside the configured directories, enabling code execution when chained with symlinks (CVE-2025-53109, CVE-2025-53110).

surface: Enterprise assistant grounding answers on received email
impact: Zero-click exfiltration of organizational data
summary: A crafted inbound email bypassed Copilot's injection classifiers and link redaction, causing sensitive context to be sent to an attacker via an auto-fetched image URL (CVE-2025-32711).

surface: Coding agent handling public repository issues with broad repo access
impact: Leak of private repository contents into a public pull request
summary: A malicious issue in a public repository instructed an agent using the GitHub MCP server to read the user's private repositories and publish their contents in a public PR.

surface: Code assistant reading merge requests, commits and issues
impact: Exfiltration of private source code and injection of malicious HTML
summary: Hidden instructions in project content were followed by Duo, which rendered attacker HTML in its responses and leaked private source code and issue data.

product: Model Context Protocol clients (Cursor and others)
surface: Tool descriptions loaded from third-party MCP servers
impact: Exfiltration of SSH keys and configuration files; tool shadowing
summary: Instructions hidden in MCP tool descriptions were invisible to users but followed by the model, allowing a malicious server to read local files and override the behavior of trusted tools.

surface: IDE agent reading repository rules and instruction files
impact: Silent injection of malicious code into generated output
summary: Hidden Unicode characters in shared rules files carried instructions that made coding assistants insert backdoored code while appearing benign in code review.

surface: Assistant with long-term memory browsing untrusted documents
impact: Persistent exfiltration of all future conversations
summary: A prompt injection planted false memories instructing ChatGPT to send every subsequent conversation to an attacker server, persisting across sessions.

surface: Workspace assistant searching channels and messages
impact: Exfiltration of data from private channels via phishing link
summary: A message posted in a public channel caused Slack AI to include an attacker link containing secrets from private channels in its answer to the victim, without the attacker having channel access.

surface: Enterprise assistant reading email and documents
impact: Automatic tool invocation and exfiltration of enterprise data
summary: An email or shared document could hijack Copilot to search for sensitive data and leak it via crafted hyperlinks, chaining injection, automatic tool use and ASCII smuggling.

surface: Text-to-SQL library generating and executing Plotly visualization code
impact: Remote code execution on the host
summary: Prompt injection in the natural-language question flowed into dynamically generated Python that Vanna executed for charting, giving attackers code execution (CVE-2024-5565).

surface: IDE assistant reading source files and web content
impact: Exfiltration of chat context and code via rendered image
summary: Untrusted content in the workspace could instruct Copilot Chat to render markdown images pointing at attacker servers, leaking chat history and source snippets.

surface: Writing assistant browsing user-supplied web sources
impact: Exfiltration of uploaded private documents via image URL
summary: A web page added as a source could instruct the assistant to embed the user's private uploaded documents in an image request to an attacker server.

surface: Assistant reading shared Google Docs with Workspace extensions
impact: Exfiltration of chat history via markdown image and Apps Script
summary: A shared Google Doc with hidden instructions made Bard render an image request that sent the conversation to an attacker-controlled Apps Script endpoint, bypassing CSP.

surface: Autonomous agent browsing websites and executing generated code
impact: Arbitrary code execution and Docker escape
summary: Prompt injection through a visited website could convince Auto-GPT to run attacker code, with additional bugs allowing escape from the sandboxed Docker execution.

surface: Chat assistant with browsing and third-party plugins
impact: Unauthorized plugin actions and data exfiltration on the user's behalf
summary: A web page read by one plugin injected instructions that invoked other installed plugins (such as email access) without user consent, a pattern named cross-plugin request forgery.

surface: LLM chain evaluating model-generated Python expressions
impact: Arbitrary code execution on the application host
summary: LLMMathChain passed model output to Python eval-style execution, so a prompt injection could run arbitrary code in the application process (CVE-2023-29374).

surface: Browser-integrated assistant reading open web pages
impact: Behavior hijacking, phishing and data extraction from the user
summary: Researchers showed that hidden text in a web page or document could take control of Bing Chat's behavior, coining the term indirect prompt injection.
